newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar extends losses,briefly falls below 114 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar extends losses,briefly falls below 114 yen.

text.p: 0131 GMT --*Dollar extended losses against yen due to slew of stop-loss dollar sales, including option-linked ones, at several points such as 114.70 yen, 114.50 yen and below.
*Dollar briefly fell as low as 113.85 yen as of 0130 GMT, its lowest level since late December 1996.

*Dollar started falling on speculation that U.S. Fed likely to keep interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting meeting later in day and that U.S. may not be worried about dollar's recent falls, dealers said. "Sentiment is dark, with trading mainly driven by technical reasons," said a bank trader.
*Both exporters and major Japanese investors taking wait-and-see attitude in face of dollar's decline, said a senior dealer at a Japanese bank.
*Dollar's relentless fall forced some operators to sell dollars to limit their losses, accelerating dollar's falls, he said. Further stops expected at 113.50 yen.
*"Stop-loss sales may emerge at every 0.50 yen fall all the way down to 110 yen," said one bank trader.
*Mark's weakness against yen becoming another factor pushing yen higher against dollar. Mark/yen has recently moved in tandem with dollar/yen, dealers said.
